name: QuIP: 2-Bit Quantization of Large Language Models With Guarantees
problem: Below 3 bits, weight quantization error explodes because weights are spread-out and the Hessian directions that matter for rounding are badly aligned with the coordinate axes.
mechanism: Quantization with Incoherence Processing, in two steps: (1) incoherence processing - multiply the weights and the inverse-Hessian by random orthogonal matrices (folded into neighbouring weight matrices so there is no inference-time cost) so weights become near-Gaussian with even magnitudes and the rounding-sensitive directions are unaligned with the axes; (2) adaptive rounding that greedily minimizes a quadratic proxy of the layer-output error, with closed-form clipping thresholds per coordinate. Ships the first theoretical analysis for an LLM-scale quantization algorithm (which also retroactively explains OPTQ).
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): incoherence preprocessing improves SEVERAL EXISTING quantization algorithms (not just its own), and yields the first LLM quantization methods producing 'viable' results at only TWO bits per weight. COMPRESSION RATIO: 8x at 2 bits/weight. QUALITY COST: the abstract deliberately says 'viable results' rather than 'no loss' - the 2-bit configuration is usable, not clean, and the paper's own framing is that this is the first demonstration rather than a production-grade point.
